description: I am an enthusiastic student interested in space, technology, and problem-solving. I am participating individually in the NASA Space Apps Challenge to learn, explore creative ideas, and build an innovative solution for the AstroMission challenge. I enjoy learning new skills and using technology to solve real-world problems. I am excited to collaborate, gain experience, and contribute my best ideas to this challenge.
summary:
PROJECT ASTROGAME is a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer designed for children aged 7-12. It transforms complex space engineering into a fun, interactive survival game.

The Problem: Most space games for kids ignore real engineering trade-offs. Our game makes those trade-offs tangible. Players manage a Lunar / Martian Outpost with only 100 Power and must divide it between Life Support (Oxygen), Radiation Shielding, and Food Production.

Gameplay: First, players make their Outpost Decision. Then, they enter a Run & Survive level where their decision comes to life. If Shield is low, Radiation rises rapidly. If Oxygen is low, Health drops rapidly. Players must collect Power Gems, Oxygen Tanks, and Food to correct their choices. In the final 150m, a Monster Chase begins with breaking bridges and jumping gaps. Each level ends with a Bubble Puzzle where players learn a new, non-repeating NASA Fact.

With 10 Missions across the Moon, Mars, Europa, ISS, and beyond, and 80+ real NASA Facts from DONKI, DSN, and OSDR, PROJECT ASTROGAME teaches a powerful lesson: real astronauts cannot have everything - they must balance, decide, and survive.
details:
WHAT DOES IT DO?

PROJECT ASTROGAME is a playable web game that teaches children aged 7-12 how to survive as a Junior Astronaut. The player manages a Lunar / Martian Outpost and must keep the crew alive while completing 10 Missions.

HOW DOES IT WORK?

The game has 4 connected stages:

1. OUTPOST DECISION: The player receives only 100 Power. They must split it between Life Support (Oxygen), Radiation Shielding, and Food Production. This is the core trade-off of the game.

2. RUN & SURVIVE: The player runs and collects Power Gems, Oxygen Tanks, and Food. Their earlier decision changes the gameplay live. If Shield is low, Radiation rises fast. If Oxygen is low, Health drops fast. Live bars show Health, Power, Oxygen, Food, Shield, and Radiation.

3. MONSTER CHASE: In the last 150m, a Monster chases the player, bridges break, and the player must jump gaps to survive.

4. BUBBLE PUZZLE: Each level ends with a puzzle. The player pops the correct bubble and learns a new NASA Fact. Facts never repeat in a run.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT:

It teaches systems thinking, decision-making, and resource management in a fun way. Instead of reading about space, kids FEEL the consequence of a bad decision. It is built for classrooms and home learning, needs no installation, and works on any phone or computer.

TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGIES USED:

We used HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for the game. GitHub Pages is used for hosting. Game data is inspired by real NASA open data sources - DONKI for solar storms, DSN for Deep Space Network, and OSDR for space biology research. No special hardware is needed.

WHAT MAKES IT CREATIVE?

We connected a strategy decision to an action runner game. Most games keep these separate. In our game, your strategy directly changes your survival difficulty. We also added 80+ real NASA Facts inside gameplay, so learning happens while playing, not by reading a textbook.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED:

We considered age-appropriateness (simple controls, bright visuals), accessibility (works on low-end devices, no download), and scientific accuracy (facts checked against NASA sources).
